la:verb:significo.gloss: to show, express, signify, point out
senses: to show, express, signify, point out
la:verb:significo.html:
signĭfĭco, āvi, ātum, 1 (
dep. collat. form signĭfĭcor, acc. to , without an example), v. a.
signum-facio
.
In gen., to show by signs; to show, point out, express, publish, make known, indicate; to intimate, notify, signify, etc. (freq. and class.; syn.: monstro, declaro, indico).
With acc.: aliquid alicui,: hoc mihi significasse et annuisse visus est,: quae significari ac declarari volemus,: gratulationem,: stultitiam,: deditionem,: timorem fremitu et concursu,: vir, quem ne inimicus quidem satis in appellando significare poterat, (13, 29): aliquid per gestum, et saep.— With two acc. (rare): ut eorum ornatus in his regem neminem significaret,; .—
With object clause: hoc tibi non significandum solum, sed etiam

declarandum arbitror, nihil mihi esse potuisse tuis litteris gratius, ; cf. : provocationem a regibus fuisse significant nostri augurales,: se esse admodum delectatos,: omnes voce significare coeperunt, sese, etc.,; ; cf.: hoc significant, sese ad statuas tuas pecuniam contulisse,.—

With rel. or interrog.-clause: neque unde, nec quo die datae essent (litterae), aut quo tempore te exspectarem, significabant,: nutu significat, quid velit,: (anseres et canes) aluntur in Capitolio, ut significent, si fures venerint, etc.,: significare coeperunt, ut dimitterentur,.—
With de: significare de fugā Romanis coeperunt,: est aliquid de virtute significatum tuā,.—(ε) Absol.: diversae state ... Neve inter vos significetis,: significare inter sese coeperunt,: ut quam maxime significem,: ut fumo atque ignibus significabatur,: ubi major atque illustrior incidit res, clamore per agros regionesque significant,.—
In partic.
To betoken, prognosticate, foreshow, portend, mean (syn. praedico): futura posse a quibusdam significari,: quid haec tanta celeritas festinatioque significat?: quid sibi significent, trepidantia consulit exta,; cf.: quid mihi significant ergo mea visa?: significet placidos nuntia fibra deos,: quae fato manent, quamvis significata, non vitantur,.—
To betoken a change of weather (post-Aug.): ventus Africus tempestatem significat, etc.,: serenos dies (luna),: imbrem (occasus Librae),, § 246.—Absol.: terreni ignes proxime significant,.—
To call, name: quod Antoninum filium suum ipse significari voluit,.—
To mean, import, signify; of words: carere hoc significat, egere eo, quod habere velis, etc.,: multa verba aliud nunc ostendunt, aliud ante significabant, ut hostis, Müll.; 9, § 85 ib.: videtis hoc uno verbo unde significare res duas, et ex quo et a quo loco,.—Of a fable: haec significat fabula dominum videre plurimum,; .— Hence, signĭfĭcans, antis, P. a., in rhet. lang., of speech, full of meaning, expressive, significant; graphic, distinct, clear: locorum dilucida et significans descriptio,: verba,; cf. ; , prooem. § 31: demonstratio,.—Transf., of orators: Atticos esse lucidos et significantes,.—Comp.: quo nihil inveniri possit significantius,; .— Sup.: significantissimum vocabulum,.—Adv.: signĭfĭcanter, clearly, distinctly, expressly, significantly, graphically: breviter ac significanter ordinem rei protulisse,: rem indicare (with proprie),: dicere (with ornate),.—Comp.: apertius, significantius dignitatem alicujus defendere,: narrare,: disponere,: appellare aliquid (with consignatius),: dicere (with probabilius),.— Sup., .

signĭfĭcātus, ūs, m.
significo

A sign, token, prognostic of coming changes of weather: tempestatum significatus. ; ; .—
Lit., meaning, import, signification of a word (syn. vis): ve particula duplicem significatum capit,. —
Transf., a name, appellation: bellis significatum dare,.

la:noun:signum.html:
signum, i, n.
perh. Sanscr. sag-, to cling to, adhere; cf. sigilla
.
In gen., a mark, token, sign, indication (very frequent in all styles and periods; cf. insigne): meo patri torulus inerit aureus Sub petaso: id signum Amphitruoni non erit,: ut eam (nutricem) adducam et signa ostendam haec, i. e. crepundia,; : ut fures earum rerum, quas ceperunt, signa commutant, etc.,; so (with notae) ; ; cf.: omne probabile aut signum est aut credibile ... Signum est, quod sub sensum aliquem cadit et quiddam significat, quod ex ipso profectum videtur, etc.,: aut pecori signum aut numeros inpressit acervis,; cf.: servitii signum cervice gerens,: jaculo mihi vulnera fecit.—Signa vides: apparet adhuc vetus ecce cicatrix,: metam Constituit signum nautis pater, unde reverti Scirent, etc.,: scutum signi gratia positum,: signa pedum,tracks, prints,; and simply signa,: oculis mihi signum dedit, Ne se appellarem,: dare,: dicere deos gallis signum dedisse cantandi,: signa esse ad salutem,: animi pudentis signum,: color pudoris signum,: signa doloris ostendere,: mortis dare,: timoris mittere,to exhibit, display, et saep.—With obj.-clause: magnum hoc quoque signum est, dominam esse extra noxiam,; .—In predic. gen. with neutr. pron.: hoc est signi; ubi primum poterit, se illinc subducet,: id erit signi me invitum facere, quod, etc.,; ; ; : nil tamen est signi,; cf.: quid signi?.— Hence, a surname, epithet (rare): huic signum exercitus apposuit,; cf. .—
In partic.
In milit. lang.
The distinctive sign of a division of an army.
A military standard, ensign, banner (including the aquila): signifero interfecto, signo amisso,: ut neque signiferi viam, nec signa milites cernerent,: Hasdrubal ut procul signa legionum fulgentia vidit,; ; : inter signa militaria,: cum unius signi militibus pergit ire,: signa militaria ex proelio relata,; so, militaria,; .— Hence the expressions: signa sequi,to follow the standards, to march in military order,; : signa subsequi,to keep in order of battle,: signa observare,: signa servare,; : ab signis discedere,to desert the standards, leave the ranks,; fin.; ; ; cf.: ab ordinibus signisque discedere,: signa relinquere,to desert,; : signa deserere,: signa ferre, i. e. to break up the camp, ; ; ; ; for which: movere signa,; ; ; and: tollere,; Auct. B. Alex. 57, 1; but: ferte signa in hostem,attack,: signa constituere,to halt,; cf.: infestis contra hostes signis constiterunt,: signa proferre,to advance,: signa convertere, to wheel, turn, or face about, ; : ; ; ; for which,

vertere signa, : signa inferre (in aliquem),to advance to the attack, make an assault,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; al; cf.: signa conferre cum aliquo,to engage with, engage in close fight,; ; and cf.: collatis signis pugnare, superare aliquem, etc.,; ; ; ; but conferre signa also means simply to bring the standards together (to one place), ; ; : signa in laevum cornu confert,concentrates his troops,: signa transferre,to desert,: signa convellere, to take up the standards, which had been fixed in the ground, ; ; ; so, vellere signa,; : revellere signa,; cf.: signa figere,to encamp,: defigere signa,: sub signis ducere legiones, ire, esse, etc.,together, in order, in rank and file, (with ordine); ; ; : signa hostium turbare,to throw into disorder,: ante signa,before the army,; ; : post signa,.—

Transf., in gen.: infestis prope signis inferuntur Galli in Fonteium, (16, 34).—
Esp., the standard or ensign of single cohorts and maniples (opp. aquila, the standard of the entire legion): cum fasces, cum tubas, cum signa militaria, cum aquilam illam argenteam ... scirem esse praemissam,; Galb. ap. ; Oud.; ; ; ; ; (cf. aquila, 2.): manipulos exercitus minimas manus quae unum sequuntur signum, Müll.—
Meton., a cohort, a maniple: octo cohortes in fronte constituit, reliquarum signa in subsidio artius collocat,; ; fin.; 33, 1; 27, 14; 28, 14; Auct. B. Hisp. 18, 3.—
A sign, signal; a watchword, password, given by a wind-instrument, by the tessera, or otherwise: signum tubā dare,; : proelii committendi dare,: recipiendi dare,: receptui dare,; ; ; cf. : signum dare ut, etc.,; : proelii exposcere,: concinere,; ; cf. : canere,; ; ; ; ; (v. cano).—For the chariot race: signum mittendis quadrigis dare,: signum mittere, Enn. ap. : signo Felicitatis dato, the word, watchword, Felicitas, Auct. B. Afr. 83: signum petere,; ; ; cf.: it bello tessera signum,.—Transf.: tu illam (virtutem) jubes signum petere,i. e. to be in subjection,.—
A sign or token of any thing to come; a prognostic, symptom (cf.: portentum, indicium): ipse et equus ejus repente concidit: nec eam rem habuit religioni, objecto signo, ut peritis videbatur, ne committeret proelium,: medici signa quaedam habent ex venis et ex spiritu aegroti,; cf. ; ; ; : prospera signa dare, (19), 152.—
An image, as a work of art; a figure, statue, picture, etc. (syn.: effigies, imago, simulacrum); inerant (classi) signa expressa, Titani quomodo, etc.,: statuas deorum, exempla earum facierum, s gna domi pro supellectile statuere, Cato ap. P.: signum pictum in pariete,: signum in fano,: aëna signa,: ante signum Jovis Statoris concidit,: signum aeneum, marmoreum, eburneum,; cf. ; : cratera impressum signis,; ; : (vestis) auro signisque ingentibus apta,: ex ornatis aedibus per aulaea et signa, Dietsch: pallam signis auroque rigentem,: e Pario formatum marmore signum,; cf. ; 12, 398: statuas, signa, picturas commendet,.—
An image or device on a seal-ring; a seal, signet: ostendi tabellas Lentulo, et quaesivi, cognosceretne signum. Annuit. Est vero, inquam, notum signum, imago avi tui, etc., : (patera) in cistulā obsignata signo est,; cf. : tabulae maximae signis hominum nobilium consignantur,: imprimat his signa tabellis,: litterae integris signis praetoribus traduntur,; : signo laeso non insanire lagenae,: volumen sub signo habere,to have under seal,; cf.: sub signo claustrisque rei publicae positum vectigal,: nec pacta conventaque inpressis signis custodirentur,: cum sol duodena peregit signa,.—
A sign in the heavens, a constellation (cf. sidus): caeli subter labentia signa,: loca caelio Omnia, dispositis signis ornata,: signorum ortus et obitus,: signis omnibus ad idem principium stellisque revocatis,: in signo leonis,: signorum obitus speculari et ortus,; : signum pluviale Capellae,: ponemusque suos ad vaga signa dies,: nox caelo diffundere signa parabat,; cf. .—
Miraculous works (eccl. Lat.), ; ; et saep.

senses: to point out, to indicate, to express, to designate
la:verb:signo.html:
signo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
signum
,
to set a mark upon, to mark, mark out, designate (syn.: noto, designo).
Lit.
In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): discrimen non facit neque signat linea alba, Lucil. ap. : signata sanguine pluma est,: ne signare quidem aut partiri limite campum Fas erat,: humum limite mensor,; : moenia aratro,: pede certo humum,to print, press,; cf.: vestigia summo pulvere,to mark, imprint,: auratā cyclade humum, . haec nostro signabitur area curru,: locum, ubi ea (cistella) excidit,: caeli regionem in cortice signant,mark, cut,: nomina saxo,: rem stilo,: rem carmine,; for which: carmine saxum,: cubitum longis litteris,: ceram figuris,to imprint,: cruor signaverat herbam,had stained,; cf. : signatum sanguine pectus,: dubiā lanugine malas,: signata in stirpe cicatrix,: manibus Procne pectus signata cruentis,: vocis infinitios sonos paucis notis,: visum objectum imprimet et quasi signabit in animo suam speciem,.—
In partic.
To mark with a seal; to seal, seal up, affix a seal to a thing (usually obsignare): accepi a te signatum libellum,: volumina,: locellum tibi signatum remisi, Caes. ap. P.: epistula,: arcanas tabellas,: signatis quicquam mandare tabellis,: lagenam (anulus),: testamentum,; cf. : nec nisi signata venumdabatur (terra),.—Absol., ; ; .—
To mark with a stamp; hence,
Of money, to stamp, to coin: aes argentum aurumve publice signanto,; cf.: qui primus ex auro denarium signavit ... Servius rex primus signavit aes ... Signatum est nota pecudum, unde et pecunia appellata ... Argentum signatum est anno, etc.,: argentum signatum,; ; : pecunia signata Illyriorum signo,: denarius signatus Victoriā,: sed cur navalis in aere Altera signata est,: milia talentūm argenti non signati formā, sed rudi pondere,.— Hence,
Poet.: signatum memori pectore nomen habe,imprinted, impressed,: (filia) quae patriā signatur imagine vultus,i. e. closely resembles her father,.—
To stamp, i. e. to license, invest with official authority (late Lat.): quidam per ampla spatia urbis ... equos velut publicos signatis, quod dicitur, calceis agitant,.—
Pregn., to distinguish, adorn, decorate (poet.): pater ipse suo superūm jam signat honore, Heyne: caelum corona, 273.—
Trop., to point out, signify, indicate, designate, express (rare; more usually significo, designo; in Cic. only Or. 19, 64, where dignata is given by ; v. Meyer ad loc.): translatio plerumque signandis rebus ac sub oculos subiciendis reperta est,: quotiens suis verbis signare nostra voluerunt (Graeci),; cf.: appellatione signare,: utrius differentiam,; cf. ; : nomen (Caieta) ossa signat,: fama signata loco est,: miratrixque sui signavit nomine terras,designated,; cf.: (Earinus) Nomine qui signat tempora verna suo,: Turnus ut videt ... So signari oculis,singled out, looked to,: signare responsum, to give a definite or distinct answer, .—With rel.-clause: memoria signat in quā regione quali adjutore legatoque fratre meo usus sit,.—
To distinguish, recognize: primi clipeos mentitaque tela Adgnoscunt, atque ora sono discordia signant,; cf.: sonis homines dignoscere,: animo signa quodcumque in corpore mendum est,.—
To seal, settle, establish, confirm, prescribe (mostly poet.): signanda sunt jura,signata jura,: jura Suevis, Claud. ap. ; cf.: precati deos ut velint ea (vota) semper solvi semperque signari, (44).—
To close, end: qui prima novo signat quinquennia lustro,.—Hence,
signan-ter, adv. (acc. to II. A.), expressly, clearly, distinctly (late Lat. for the class. significanter): signanter et breviter omnia indicare,: signanter et proprie dixerat,—
signātus, a, um, P. a.
(Acc. to I. B. 1. sealed; hence) Shut up, guarded, preserved (mostly ante- and post-class.): signata sacra, Varr. ap. : limina. . Chrysidem negat signatam reddere, i. e. unharmed, intact, pure, Lucil. ap. ; cf.: assume de viduis fide pulchram, aetate signatam,.—
(Acc. to II. A.) Plain, clear, manifest (post-class. for significans): quid expressius atque signatius in hanc causam?.—Adv.: signātē, clearly, distinctly (post-class.): qui (veteres) proprie atque signate locuti sunt,; .—Comp.: signatius explicare aliquid,.

Sīgēum, i, n., = Σίγειον,
a promontory in Troas, and a town of the same name, where Achilles was buried, now Yenishehr, ; ; ; ; .—Hence, Sīgēus (collat. form Sīgēïatellus, : Sigeïa litora,), a, um, adj., of or belonging to Sigeum, Sigean: litora,; : freta,: campi,: profundum,.
Poet. transf., Trojan: natum Sigeo in pulvere,i.e. in the Trojan war,.—
Roman: colonus,.

la:noun:significatio.html:
signĭfĭcātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
.
A pointing out, indicating, denoting, signifying; an expression, indication, mark, sign, token, = indicium, signum, ἐπισημασία, etc. (freq. and class.).
Absol.: gestus sententiam non demonstratione sed significatione declarans,: aliquem nutu significationeque appellare,: ignibus significatione factā. 2, 33: significatione per castella fumo factā,; .—With subj. gen.: ex significatione Gallorum,: litterarum,.—
With obj. gen. (so most freq.): voluntatis,: victoriae,: adventus,fin.: virtutis,; cf. : significatio calamitatum,: artificii,: probitatis,; et saep.—Plur.: valetudinis significationes,: rerum futurarum,. —
With object-clause (very rare): ex quibus magna significatio fit, non adesse constantiam,.—Plur.: multas nec dubias significationes saepe jecit: ne reliquis quidem se parsurum senatoribus,.—
In partic.
Pregn., like the Gr. ἐπισημασία, a sign or token of assent, an expression of approbation, applause: populi judiciis atque omni significatione florere,; cf. ; 59, 127: ut ex ipsā significatione potuit cognosci,.— Plur., : significationibus acclamationibus multitudinis, (corresp. to assentatio).—
Also, like ἐπισημασία, a sign, token, foretoken, prognostic of the weather (Plinian): est et aquarum significatio, etc.... caeli quidem murmur non dubiam habet significationem. Praesagiunt et animalia,—
In rhet. lang., significance, emphasis: significatio est, quae plus in suspicione relinquit, quam positum est in oratione,; ; ; (as a transl. of the Gr. ἔμφασις).—
In gram., meaning, sense, import, signification of a word or phrase: verbi, Müll.: scripti,; cf. : est igitur tropus sermo a naturali et principali significatione translatus ad aliam,: ejusdem verbi contraria significatio,: voces eaedem diversā in significatione ponuntur,: verborum,: latens,: propriae,.—So the titles of the lexical works of Aelius Gallus, Verrius Flaccus, Festus, etc.: De verborum Significatione or Significationibus.—
Meaning, intent: duas significationes habet propositio vestra,includes two assertions,.

Bearing the heavenly signs or constellations, starry: aether,: caelum,; : orbis, qui Graece ζωδιακὸς dicitur, the zodiac, ; so, orbis,; ; for which also, polus,; ; and subst. signifer, the sky, the heavens, etc., ; ; ; ; —
